fields.value: Fine dark eyes and a light, pleasing figure; the novel gives selective impressions rather than a fixed portrait.
Quick-witted, playful, observant, independent, and capable of strong prejudice when vanity and partial evidence align.
To preserve self-respect and marry only where affection and esteem make happiness plausible.
Second of the five Bennet daughters, raised at Longbourn in a loving but socially precarious landed family.
Twenty; she tells Lady Catherine that she is not yet one-and-twenty.
Protagonist and primary centre of perception.
Daughter of Mr and Mrs Bennet; closest to Jane; niece of Mr and Mrs Gardiner.
Moves from confident first impressions to self-knowledge, fairer judgment, and a love grounded in observed conduct.
Darcy: adversarial attraction to mutual respect. Jane: trusted sister. Wickham: misplaced confidence. Gardiners: affectionate guides.
